Posterior predictive intervals on a fitted mvgam model

Source: R/brms_wrappers.mvgam.R
predictive_interval.mvgam.Rd

Central quantile intervals of the draws posterior_predict.mvgam() returns, one per observation.

Usage

# S3 method for mvgam
predictive_interval(object, prob = 0.9, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted mvgam object.

prob

Numeric in (0, 1). The probability mass each interval holds. Defaults to 0.9.

...

Arguments of posterior_predict.mvgam(), such as newdata or incl_autocor.

Value

A numeric matrix with one row per observation and two columns, the lower and upper bounds.

See also

posterior_interval.mvgam() gives intervals of parameters. pp_check.mvgam() plots predictive draws against the data.

Other predictions: conditional_effects.mvgam(), conditional_smooths.mvgam(), fitted.mvgam(), hindcast.mvgam(), posterior_epred.mvgam(), posterior_linpred.mvgam(), posterior_predict.mvgam(), posterior_smooths.mvgam(), predict.mvgam(), predictive_error.mvgam()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
             data = simdat$data_train, family = poisson(),
             chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 9 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# 90 percent intervals, one row per observation
intervals <- predictive_interval(mod)
head(intervals)
#>      5%   95%
#> [1,]  0  5.00
#> [2,]  7 23.00
#> [3,]  3 13.05
#> [4,]  4 14.00
#> [5,]  1  9.00
#> [6,]  2 14.00

# The share of observed counts the intervals cover
y <- simdat$data_train$y
mean(y >= intervals[, 1] & y <= intervals[, 2])
#> [1] 0.8

# Next: pp_check() plots the predictive draws against the data
# }
